Follow P → Q, D → J, Q → P, J → D twice. The third identical position is a draw. Nearby draw offers also need explicit opponent acceptance.

Start with three tigers at A, D and E; fifteen lambs wait off the board. Lambs play first.

During placement, add one lamb to any empty point. Tigers move or capture between placements. Captured lambs never return to reserve.

Once all fifteen have been placed, lambs move one edge to an empty point. Tigers also move one edge, or jump straight over one lamb to the next empty point. Captures are optional. No turns during a jump, no jumping tigers, and no chained captures. N–T and S–W are not edges.

Tigers win immediately after five captures. Lambs win when all three tigers have no legal step or capture. Check wins before draws.

The third identical position is a draw: same species occupancy, next side, phase, reserve and captured counts. Nearby players may agree a draw only with explicit acceptance. Leaving or losing a connection creates no result.

Solo Hint suggests one legal action; it does not promise the best move. Undo on your turn removes your previous action and its computer reply. Invalid state blocks play; there is no pass or automatic result.
